chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mature woman (thayyib) who proposes marriage to herself. He said: 'She has more authority over herself; she may appoint whomever she wishes to manage her affairs, provided she has previously been married to a husband.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has more authority/power over herself
key_terms.اَلثَّيِّبُ: A mature woman who has previously been married and consummated the marriage
key_terms.تُوَلِّي أَمْرَهَا: She appoints someone to manage her affairs (specifically the marriage contract)

ai.seo_question: Does a mature woman need a male guardian to contract her own marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a *thayyib* (mature woman with prior marriage experience), distinguishing her from a *bikr* (virgin) who typically requires a guardian's consent. It establishes that her autonomy (*amlak*) allows her to either contract marriage directly or appoint a proxy of her choice, reflecting the Shia juristic view that prior marriage confers full legal capacity. This ruling underscores the principle of female agency in marital contracts within the framework of *usul al-fiqh*.
